claim: Figure S6A and Figure S6B report the same quantity for the same four lipidoids at the same nominal dose, so they should agree.
what_we_measured: Ratio B/A = 1.281 / 0.577 / 0.519 / 0.499. The RANK INVERTS: S6A orders O10>O11>O12>Oi10, S6B orders Oi10>O10>O11>O12, Spearman rho = -0.20 on 4 points. Both panels are HeLa / unmodified FLuc mRNA / RLU / 24 h / n=4 and S6A's single dose IS 100 ng. The three non-Oi10 ratios cluster at 0.50-0.58 while Oi10's is 1.28, so it is not one scale factor.
what_we_emitted: Figure S6A only, as KW_2019. Figure S6B's 12 values are in 05_values.csv flagged emitted_to_06_rows=no with this reason. NEITHER panel is averaged into the other and neither is rescaled by the other.
status: CONFIRMED -- a real within-paper, within-lab, same-dose disagreement. Queued as D-3.

claim: SI Methods p.2: 'mixing lipidoid, cholesterol, ... DOPE ..., C14-PEG2000 ..., at a molar ratio of 35 : 16 : 46.5 : 2.5'. Read positionally: cholesterol 16 mol%, DOPE 46.5 mol%.
locus_A: SI p.2, Formulation of LNPs, component list order vs ratio order
locus_B: data/data_vitro.csv + data/data_vivo.csv: 20 experiments use this exact 35/x/y/2.5 ratio and EVERY one assigns helper lipid 16 / cholesterol 46.5. Zero rows in all 29,195+1,803 have CHL_molratio 16 or HL_molratio 46.5. AC_2025 varies the pair (28/34.5, 8/54.5, 16/46.5, 50/12.5) always summing to 62.5. BL_2023_3CR uses the identical printed reagent name C14-PEG2000 with DOPE 16 / cholesterol 46.5. Separately, the same lab's 2024 paper staged at curation/whiteheadka_38888972 records its Methods as 'lipidoid : cholesterol : DOPE : PEG2000 = 35 : 46.5 : 16 : 2.5'.
what_we_measured: The four percentages sum to exactly 100 either way, so the SUM cannot discriminate and nothing else in this SI can. The mapping is what is in doubt, not the numbers. 20/20 merged corpus experiments and the lab's own later Methods sentence both put cholesterol at 46.5.
what_we_emitted: HL(DOPE)=16, CHL(Cholesterol)=46.5 -- the corpus convention -- with the discrepancy named in curation_note on all 11 rows. Chosen this way because an excipient field that differs from every other experiment for a prose-ordering reason would manufacture exactly the source-separability signal this project exists to measure.
status: CONFIRMED discrepancy, NOT resolved here. Queued as D-1; the merge is blocked on it.

claim: Table S1's pKa and Table S2's 'Average pKa' are the same quantity for the same lipidoids and should agree.
locus_A: SI p.6 Table S1 'pKa' (LNP surface pKa, TNS fluorescence titration on assembled LNPs in aqueous buffer, SI p.3)
locus_B: SI p.15 Table S2 'Average pKa' (lipidoid pKa, Henderson-Hasselbalch from 0.1 M HCl titration of free lipidoid in ETHANOL, SI pp.2, 16-17)
what_we_measured: They differ by up to 1.14 pH units (306O14: 7.44 vs 6.30); 7 of 10 differ by more than 0.3; mean signed difference +0.27. The two methods also disagree on direction: Table S1 makes 306Oi10 the LOWEST pKa of the family (6.40, the paper's whole mechanistic argument) while Table S2 puts it mid-pack (7.30).
what_we_emitted: Neither -- pKa is a physicochemical property, not a delivery endpoint, and the corpus excludes that class. Both tables extracted to 04_table_s1.csv / 04_table_s2.csv and the gap recorded so nobody pools or averages them.
status: RETIRED as a contradiction by reading the two Methods paragraphs: different material, different solvent, different method. Kept because a reader who pooled the two columns would silently destroy the paper's central claim.

claim: Figure S4's six-colour organ legend means six bars per dose, so a bar top is one organ's signal.
locus_A: SI p.10 Fig S4 legend: Liver / Spleen / Lungs / Heart / Kidneys / Pancreas
locus_B: SI p.10 path geometry: exactly ONE 23.01 pt bar per x category, with 4 categories (Crl + 0.25 + 0.75 + 1.5 mg/kg) and multiple near-coincident horizontal rules inside each bar; 11.42 pt rules are the error-bar caps (half width).
what_we_measured: Fig S4 is a STACKED bar chart: the six organs are summed within one bar per dose, so the drawn bar top is the six-organ TOTAL, not the liver. 2 lipidoids x 3 doses = 6 total-flux values and 36 organ segments.
what_we_emitted: Nothing -- Fig S4 was not digitised (D-2). The structural measurement is recorded so that if it is ever digitised nobody reads a stack top as an organ.
status: RETIRED by measurement. My initial reading of the legend was wrong.

claim: 306O18 has no bar in Figure S6A (no fill rectangle is present at its x tick).
locus_A: SI p.12: the 11 series-blue fill rects stop at x 272.40 (306O16); at 306O18's slot there is only a 2.80 pt TEAL square at (285.20, 216.81)-(288.00, 219.60).
locus_B: SI p.12: a full 8.51 pt bar OUTLINE spanning x 285.22-293.73 with its top rule at y 219.581, plus a 4.19 pt error-bar cap at y 219.406.

Its fill is rendered as a 2.80 pt pattern tile in a different colour instead of the series blue -- the same 2.80 pt tile size GraphPad uses for Figure S6B's hatched series markers. claim: The category-to-bar assignment in Figure S6A may be off by one slot, because the '****' significance label sits far from the bracket it should annotate.
locus_A: SI p.12: '****' text centred at x 217.3 pt; the only unassigned bracket spans x 148.12-201.45 with its rule at y 104.36, midpoint 174.8 pt -- the label is 42.5 pt away from it.
locus_B: SI p.12: 14 x-axis TICK MARKS on a 12.81 pt pitch (spread 0.061 pt); every bar centre lands on a tick to <=0.059 pt; all 11 horizontal O-labels' right edges sit at tick + 2.994 pt with a spread of 0.002 pt. The '**' bracket's legs land on the Lipo MM tick (148.53) and the 306O8 tick (174.17).
what_we_measured: The assignment is right: a one-slot error would be 12.81 pt, 6,400x the 0.002 pt label-offset spread, and the seeded one-slot rotation scores 0/11 on the absolute nearest-tick test. The '****' TEXT is a hand-placed annotation object and its position carries no information. The '**' bracket pairs Lipo MM with 306O8. The '****' bracket cannot be attributed: its left leg is on Lipo MM's tick, its right leg's x (201.45) is nearest 306Oi10's tick (199.80), but that leg's bottom (116.81 pt) sits just above 306O10's error cap (122.92) and nowhere near 306Oi10's (156.21).
what_we_emitted: The assignment as given by the ticks. No significance annotation is emitted.
status: RETIRED for the assignment. The '****' bracket's referent is UNRESOLVED and not load-bearing for any value.

claim: (my own error) The category-assignment check in stage07_seeded_checks.py discriminates a one-slot misassignment.
locus_A: First version: counted labels whose offset was within 0.05 pt of the MEAN offset of the same set.
locus_B: Seeded run with the category list rotated one slot: 11/11 clean and 11/11 seeded.
what_we_measured: The metric was shift-invariant, because rotating the list moves every offset by the same 12.81 pt and leaves the spread about the new mean unchanged. The check could not fail. Replaced with an absolute criterion -- each label's right edge within half a category pitch (6.40 pt) of its assigned tick -- which scores 11/11 clean and 0/11 seeded.
status: RETIRED by the seeded run. Same shape as the C16 incident ('my first two versions of C16 reported all derived while examining nothing'); it was caught only because this folder requires the agreement count to MOVE, not merely to raise.

claim: (my own error) IL_tail1_SMILES held the tail acrylate reagent.
locus_A: First version of stage06_rows.py: '"C=CC(=O)" + alcohol_SMILES', which for hexan-1-ol ('CCCCCCO', O terminal) produced 'C=CC(=O)CCCCCCO'.
locus_B: That string is a ketone bearing a free primary alcohol, not an acrylate ester. It parses, canonicalises and has a plausible formula.
what_we_measured: All 11 tail columns were wrong. Rebuilt through curation/lib assemble.esterify('C=CC(=O)O', alcohol); the 11 now read C=CC(=O)OCCCCCC ... C=CC(=O)OCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC and A306_O10's matches the corpus convention 'C=CC(=O)OCCCCCCCCCC' exactly.
status: RETIRED. The string surgery was two lines above my own comment warning against string surgery; it was caught by printing the column, not by any check.

claim: (found en route, NOT this paper) 'DMPE-PEG2000' names one structure in the corpus.
locus_A: curation/lib reagents.smi('DMPE-PEG2000') REFUSED: the name carries 2 different structures across experiments.
locus_B: One is a dimyristoyl-glycerol PEG ETHER (DMG-PEG chemistry, no phosphate); the other is a true phosphoethanolamine-PEG with a phosphate and an amide linker.
what_we_measured: Not this paper's problem -- this paper prints 'C14-PEG2000', which resolves uniquely in the corpus. Reported only because the refusal happened while resolving this paper's excipients and the guard worked exactly as designed.
what_we_emitted: C14-PEG2000's unique corpus structure. PEG block length is a distribution, so the stored number of EO units is a convention either way (CLAUDE.md: PEG-lipids are deliberately absent from the reagent registry).
status: REPORTED, not acted on. A corpus-level observation for whoever runs C17 next.
